threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus at the stop, but everyone else just walks away as soon as the screen shows 'delayed'.
Last night, the N68 rolled past a group of artists painting a mural while a couple loudly debated the merits of jellied eels. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was part of Neukölln was when I found a lively pop-up flea market in an old church, full of locals haggling over vintage records.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Spotted a kiosk selling only Spätzle and radler on a rainy day. Perfectly Berlin – the most unexpected cravings served up at odd hours.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows to dodge the Civic Center BART like it’s a minefield after 5. That station’s starting to feel like a ghost town.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a dog just lounging on the tracks at Civic Center, totally unfazed. Only in SF would a pup cause such chaos on Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists love to snap photos of the street art, but miss the local cafes where the real conversations happen over a bocadillo.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they hesitate at crosswalks, waiting for the green light when locals just dart across.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'short walk' means 10 minutes, not 30 with all the potholes and dodging hipsters on scooters.
Last night on the 12 bus, a guy argued passionately with a lamppost for five minutes before sitting down beside it like an old friend.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when the baker down the street had my order ready without me saying a word. Nothing like that warm, fresh bread smell wafting through the air.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you casually stroll past a techno club that opens at 6 AM and see people still in their pajamas, clutching their breakfast beers.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by the way they automatically dodge the BART delays while checking Muni apps. Outsiders just stand there confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus stuck under the Civic Center BART, while a guy in a tutu was waiting at the stop like it was totally normal.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all tapas are great; locals know that the best ones are hidden in corner bars where the staff remember your name.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they order 'pan con tomate'—most say it with a thick accent, like it's a brand new secret.
